title: Why Traps Lose Water and Allow Sewer Gas Odors
description: When a drainage system lacks proper venting, flowing wastewater creates a vacuum effect known as siphonage. As water rushes down the branch line, it pulls air behind it. Without a vent pipe to equalize atmospheric pressure with the outside air, negative pressure pulls standing water straight out of nearby P-traps. Once the P-trap loses its water seal, sewer gases and foul odors freely enter living spaces. Proper venting prevents pressure imbalances, ensuring that traps retain their water seal and function correctly under normal discharge conditions.

Why Traps Lose Water and Allow Sewer Gas Odors

When a drainage system lacks proper venting, flowing wastewater creates a vacuum effect known as siphonage. As water rushes down the branch line, it pulls air behind it. Without a vent pipe to equalize atmospheric pressure with the outside air, negative pressure pulls standing water straight out of nearby P-traps. Once the P-trap loses its water seal, sewer gases and foul odors freely enter living spaces. Proper venting prevents pressure imbalances, ensuring that traps retain their water seal and function correctly under normal discharge conditions.
